reply.title: At the Top of a Vertical Throw
reply.story:
When you toss a ball straight up into the air, it slows down as it climbs, stops for a fleeting moment at its highest point, and then speeds up as it falls back down. Watching it pause at the top, it is tempting to think that everything stops—that both its speed and its rate of change are zero at that single instant.

Yet, gravity never takes a break. Even when the ball is momentarily motionless at the apex, the pull of gravity is still acting on it with the exact same strength as when it left your hand. This puzzle explores what actually happens to velocity and acceleration at the very top of the flight.
reply.cardDescription: Explore a ball thrown straight up. See how velocity changes sign while acceleration remains constant at $-gravity$, even at the apex where velocity is zero.
reply.instructions: Adjust the launch speed slider to change the throw. Press Play or use the timeline scrubber to watch the motion and see how velocity and acceleration behave.
